source.publisher: Fermanagh Herald (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: Returned unopposed; the Herald of 24 May 1952 lists the members of the new Council and reports one contest only, at Newtownbutler. Original citation restored 6 Nov 2026 (the 5 Nov verification had moved it because of a text-cleaning fault).

note: Triennial election of Fermanagh County Council, polled Thursday 5 June 1952 (Belfast News-Letter, 6 June 1952: polling 'took place yesterday in Northern Ireland'). The only county council contest was Newtownbutler; the other eighteen divisions were uncontested and are named in the Herald list of 24 May 1952. The printed list contains nineteen divisions; Florencecourt, present in 1939, is not among them, but the News-Letter's 21 May 1952 nominations report says there were only three changes in the personnel of the Council, so its sitting member (the Earl of Enniskillen) was returned again. Structure and division names for the 1966-67 amalgamation are in notes/fermanagh-fcra-1969.md, from Fermanagh CRA, 'Fermanagh Facts' (1969). That is an advocacy pamphlet: use it for names only, not figures. Its register figures are disputed by Kingsley (2021) on the Omagh Rural District scheme. Read the page image before recording any number from it. Returned unopposed.
